newsitem.title: USA: LIFFE chairman sees CBOT link starting on time.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE chairman sees CBOT link starting on time.

text.p: London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) chairman Jack Wigglesworth said the exchange's link-up with the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) will start on time despite a new proposal by CBOT directors on after-hours trading systems.

"This is no big thing in the sense that we're determined to make the link work on time and we're just having to make adjustments to the existing agreement within that timeframe," Wigglesworth said in an interview.

CBOT directors on Tuesday voted to ask LIFFE to amend their agreement to trade each other's leading government bond derivatives on their open-outcry floors. Under the new proposal, trading hours for each exchange's after-hours electronics trading systems would be extended beyond the original agreement, overlapping with the trading hours of the new open-outcry sessions.
That proposal was widely seen stemming from CBOT's desire to keep the rapidly growing business on its Project A after-hours electronic trading system in the past few years.
Wigglesworth, in Tucson for a business conference on risk management, noted that he had already briefly discussed the issue with CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor, who was also at the conference.

"Chairman Arbor and I are determined that the link will go ahead on May 9 for the mutual benefit of both our members," he said. "We are two friendly exchanges. We will get together to talk about this and...further proposals. It may be to the advantage of the link."
"But any changes to the original agreement can only be made with mutual agreement," he added.
He said LIFFE did not intend to hold any emergency board meetings merely to discuss the new CBOT proposal and added that he did not know how LIFFE directors would respond.
Asked if a linkup between LIFFE's APT after-hours system and CBOT's Project A was possible, he said it had not been discussed.

"The question of whether there will be any link between the electronic systems...is more secondary, really, to the fundamental question of what trades at what time, whether it's open-outcry or electronic trading," Wigglesworth said.

He added that plans to link the two exchanges' wheat products were lower on the agenda at the moment because resources were being dedicated to preparation of a single European currency and the bond contract link-up, as well as work related to LIFFE's merger with the London Commodity Exchange last September.
Asked if a wheat contract linkage could take place later this year as the industry had previously expected, he said: "It's unlikely to be as early as that."
